logo.description: A New England town-line sign: a white panel with a black keyline border and a double-arched top edge (two humps meeting in a centre dip, like an open book). Inside: CAPE COD in heavy, wide, geometric uppercase sans set on an upward arc; a solid blue whale fluke (tail) in the centre; EST. to the left and 2018 to the right in smaller condensed uppercase sans; CANNABIS in the same heavy uppercase sans, set straight, below the tail. Lettering and border are black (#000000 in the PNGs, about #241F21 in the lossy WebPs); panel is white; the tail is the only colour, #24A3DC. Some versions add a soft grey drop shadow outside the panel. The favicon is the whale tail alone on transparency. The lettering typeface is outlined artwork and is not identified (UNVERIFIED); it is not Roboto.

directions.name: Seashore Glass (daylight town-line sign)
directions.summary: Bright, airy, beach-day mood taken straight from the og:image (the sign over a turquoise beach) and the header's whale-tail pattern on #C0E9FA. Backgrounds are layered sky-to-sea gradients and real Cape scenery; content sits on frosted white glass panels whose top edge borrows the sign's double-arched silhouette, so every card reads as a small town sign. Black Roboto type on white glass, #015375 for links and button hover, #02A7EB reserved for large fills, outlines and the glow behind the whale tail. Depth comes from three planes: a slow-parallax photo or gradient back plane, the glass middle plane, and a front plane of cut-out product jars, dune grass and the lighthouse that break out of the glass and over section seams. The whale-tail tile becomes a faint watermark that drifts at a different speed from the content. Motion is a calm 'tide' reveal (content rising from below a soft wave mask) and gentle 4-6 px hover lifts with a stronger shadow. Signature motif: the arched sign top as card, badge and section-divider shape (echoing the site's existing 'book' divider).

directions.name: Outer Cape After Dark (smoked glass, neon tide)
directions.summary: An evening version of the brand built on the existing accent #015375 deepened toward night navy, and on the site's own neon imagery (the cyan-to-magenta cannabis macro on the home background, the dark navy promo banners). Surfaces are smoked dark glass with a thin cyan rim light in #02A7EB, so the blue finally reads as light rather than as low-contrast text. The white sign logo sits on its own white plate and glows like a lit roadside sign, which keeps it unaltered. Depth comes from glowing product and bud cut-outs that overlap panel edges, soft bokeh orbs on a back plane and a horizon line of moonlit water. Offers, Moonrock Mondays-style bundles and the Loyalty VIP band suit this mood best. Motion: slow gradient drift in the background, a light sweep across glass on hover, counters for '900+ Google Reviews' and '4.9' that tick up once. Risk to manage: keep it adult and calm, never club-flyer; body text stays light on dark at AA or better.

directions.name: Route 6 Postcard (road-trip destination)
directions.summary: Builds the whole site around the line the brand repeats on every page, 'Always worth the trip!', and the town pages' 'Just a short drive down Route 6'. The mood is a sunny road trip: layered postcards, photo prints and ticket-like glass cards stacked at slight angles, with the real storefront photo (whale-tail window decals, whale-tail cones) as the hero destination. Glass is clear window glass with frosted 'decal' areas, like the shop windows, over warm sand and sea tones sampled from the brand's beach photography, with #02A7EB and the whale tail as the wayfinding colour. Depth: photos and the sign pin out of frames and overlap the next section, and a dotted Route 6 line runs down the page linking sections and the served-towns list. Motion: the route line draws itself on scroll, cards settle into place like dealt postcards, and hover tilts a card a few degrees with a parallax shift inside it. Type: Roboto at heavy weights for headlines, Roboto text, Playball only for the hand-written sign-off 'Thank you Cape Cod!'. Signature motif: route markers and mile-post counters ('Serving Cape Cod Since 2021', 'Est. 2018').
